beats.text: Quick test. Say the color of each word, not the word itself. Out loud.
Slower? Did you stumble? Almost everyone does.
Your brain reads automatically. It reads the word before you can stop it, and then it has to fight itself.
It's called the Stroop effect. First described in nineteen thirty-five, and it still catches almost everyone.
You can't not read. Try it on a friend.

sources: Stroop (1935). Studies of interference in serial verbal reactions. Journal of Experimental Psychology 18(6). Naming the ink colour of incongruent colour words takes significantly longer than naming colour patches; attributed to automatic reading. Via Wikipedia / APA.
